title: Primero Dios
desc: Every plan anybody makes has a condition attached to it
setting: You are agreeing a time with doña Chepa and she keeps adding two words to the end.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Mañana le traigo el queso, primero Dios.
steps.en: I will bring you the cheese tomorrow, God willing.

options.es: Primero Dios, doña. Aquí la espero.
options.en: God willing, doña. I will wait for you here.
options.feedback: Say it back. It is not a religious statement so much as the way a plan is closed here, and leaving it out sounds abrupt.
Agreed and fine. You answered the plan and not the phrase.

options.en: And if God does not want to?
options.feedback: It is a joke you can make in year three, not in month five. Right now it lands as making fun of her.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Si Dios me da vida, le hago un quesillo también.
steps.en: If God grants me life, I will make you a quesillo as well.

options.es: Que Dios le dé mucha, doña.
options.en: May He grant you plenty, doña.
options.feedback: You answered inside her own words. That is worth more here than any compliment you could have invented.
Warm and safe. There was an opening there and you walked past it.
She was not asking for a medical opinion. Si Dios me da vida is a formula, not a worry.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: ¿Y usted va a misa el domingo?
steps.en: And are you going to mass on Sunday?

options.es: Casi no voy, doña, pero respeto mucho.
options.en: I hardly go, doña, but I have a lot of respect for it.
options.feedback: Honest and not dismissive. Nobody needs you to believe, and everybody notices if you sneer.
Vague enough to end it. She was making conversation, not counting attendance.

options.en: I do not believe in that.
options.feedback: In a country this Catholic that is a sentence with a lot of weight in it, said to a woman who feeds you.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Ay, mijo. Bueno, nos vemos mañana, si Dios quiere.
steps.en: Oh, love. Well, see you tomorrow, God willing.

options.es: Si Dios quiere, doña. Que le vaya bien.
options.feedback: Two formulas, both hers, both returned. This is what fluency actually looks like from the outside.
Perfectly normal. You have now heard the phrase four times and not used it once.

options.es: Entonces mañana a las tres en punto.
options.en: Tomorrow at three o'clock sharp, then.
options.feedback: Nailing it to a minute is exactly what her two words exist to avoid. Nothing here is agreed that firmly, and pretending otherwise only sets you up to be annoyed.
